Extend current withDeadline/nextCalls enforcement to structured as well as reviewer-session calls for these timed code-review jobs, while retaining unrelated design-review semantics. At dispatch use min(existing per-call timeout, child remaining, root remaining); check signals/deadlines before and after calls/stages and immediately before final artifact publication. Late valid output is rejected, never stamped. Abort outstanding CLI/provider work on deadline/cancel using the existing signal path; await owned shutdown before terminal cleanup. Keep idle/stall watchdog separate, reset only on real progress, never on status polls. Remove fixed overall wait ceilings for this timed route: existing 4h total, 20/30min outer caps and CLI constructor limits must not truncate a healthy derived budget. Retain existing shorter per-call and idle limits as explicitly different failure causes; root budget is an upper bound, not a promise to tolerate a hung call. Absolute timestamps and bounded timer slices avoid Node timer overflow; no arbitrary chunk-count ceiling or budget clamp. [c20] [c21]

Extend existing codeReview.run IPC request additively with operation?:start|status|cancel and reviewHandle?:string. Omission preserves legacy streaming behavior; the new step path uses operation:start. Admission resolves scope, source fingerprint and independent reviewer before creating an in-memory daemon-owned operation with opaque unguessable handle, daemon epoch, AbortController, prepared timing plan, progress and eventual outcome. One target/source fingerprint owns at most one active review: repeated start joins it; different source fingerprint for the same active target returns review-conflict instead of competing artifact writers. Operation owns model execution, not a socket/request AbortSignal. Socket/host timeout detaches only the waiter. Explicit cancel aborts the operation and prevents final publication. status/cancel require handle plus matching repo/target; handles carry no source text or credentials. Status is read-only and never reexecutes models or replans. Every control request returns a terminal stream frame within 200 seconds: {status:pending,reviewHandle,progress,timing?} or cached existing final outcome/error. Timing is absent while preparation is incomplete and shown once frozen. insrc_code_review_step keeps phase:start and adds a discriminated pending-review state variant containing the handle/target/epoch; returns next:review_pending,state and guidance to call start with that state. In pending-review state proceed:false means explicit cancellation; in existing freshness state proceed:false retains degraded diff fallback. Update schema/help/guide with this distinction; no session-bound review gate bypass. Poll once per bounded tool turn; no duplicate start on host timeout. Active operation handles are held in the runtime registry independent of the shared one-hour step token TTL/LRU. Pending continuation tokens are pinned/refreshed until operation deadline plus a 10-minute terminal grace; during preparation idle watchdog bounds lifetime. Terminal outcomes are retained for that grace then evicted, active operations are never LRU-evicted. Daemon restart reports lost operation, never completion; new review requires fresh explicit start. Only the existing validated final run writes CR, once, under ownership and signal/deadline checks. No persistent DB or new general workflow runner. [c21] [c22] In src/shared/review-stream.ts retain CodeReviewStreamResult {runId,artifact} for legacy streams, add CodeReviewControlParams as a discriminated union: start carries operation:start plus normal target/grounding fields; status/cancel carry operation and reviewHandle plus matching repo/epicHash/storyId. Extend codeReviewRequestParams to preserve validated operation/reviewHandle rather than reconstructing and dropping them. Add CodeReviewControlResult = {status:pending,reviewHandle,progress,timing?} | {status:done,reviewHandle,result:CodeReviewStreamResult} | {status:failed,reviewHandle,error,reason} | {status:cancelled,reviewHandle}. Add codeReviewControl(params,opts):Promise<CodeReviewControlResult> alongside codeReviewStream in both StepDaemonClient and socket exports; both use the same serializer and discriminate/validate terminal frame data at runtime. The existing legacy codeReviewStream remains final-only. The step switches on status: only done.result enters existing artifact/independent-review validation; pending returns continuation, failed/cancelled report no CR. runReviewStream transport cancel still closes/aborts the request waiter, but the operation-mode handler deliberately detaches this signal from operation execution; legacy stream cancellation stays unchanged. Both transports test the same request/reply fixtures, pending requires no artifact, and malformed done cannot be accepted. Final publication additionally requires fresh source/approved-contract/BUILD fingerprint and author revalidation through the mandatory production hook; see Review input identity and publication revalidation. An unchanged start handle is not proof that inputs remained current.

dataModel.entity: Budget-aware diff partition and refusal recovery
dataModel.details: Add fitDiffMaterial(sourceSnapshot,dimensionSpec,effectiveLimitChars,revision):ReviewMaterial in a diff-fragment material helper reused by prepareDimensionJob. The immutable snapshot retains complete parent evidence; each dimension owns a derived material view, never mutates the shared snapshot. Render the real candidate singleton chunk including complete context, parent descriptors, envelope and schema. Starting with <=16Ki staging spans, recursively halve an oversized text range at Unicode-safe boundaries, regenerate full index/count/coordinates/digests and all affected obligations/adjacency, then remeasure. Pack only after every required singleton fits. Measure fixed framing with a minimal nonempty Unicode span: if even that cannot fit, explicitly refuse irreducible context; no recursion without size progress. Initial primary count is frozen only after this fit+packing. On a provider size refusal, the existing atom-only redivide path must intercept a singleton diff fragment: derive a smaller descendant material revision from the SAME original evidence using the refused cap and the same fitting function. Restart only that dimension as a new revision/job with new call IDs, discarding its old model outputs/notes/findings (never combine old and new ownership); abort/await any owned call first. Retain frozen root/child deadlines, original primary count/budget and a replacement-lineage record. All other dimensions retain their prepared source view; execute revisions serially. Descendant IDs include original parent, absolute range and revision digest; every revision still partitions the original text without gaps/overlap. Rebuild stage closures, chunk material, obligations and parent notes consistently; adapters cannot retain stale cached material. The original primary IDs remain audit/timing provenance and map to descendant ranges, not new budget credits. Repeated refusals must strictly reduce offending text range/cap or terminate. No whole-file reread, byte loss, uncontrolled snapshot change, reused invalid notes or deadline extension. Non-diff indivisible atoms retain named AtomTooLargeError. If time expires during replacement, no completed CR. [c23]

Quality fragment rows represent ranges, not independent symbols. In code-review-duplicates.ts exclude all rows carrying diff-fragment metadata from descriptionsOf/compareStage/pairStage symbol candidates; validate/reject fragment IDs injected into those pair answers. Ordinary graph/small unfragmented symbol comparisons retain existing semantics. Do not create every sibling pair or every fragment-to-foreign-symbol pair. Parent quality adjudication explicitly checks duplication among that parent fragments using all required notes. Add one diff-duplication check-item obligation for the whole fragmented diff scope, owning every diff-fragment ID (and bounded descriptions of nonfragment changed evidence), separate from per-parent obligations. Require keyed duplication facts in each fragment note, preserving source ranges, logical behavior and potential counterpart identifiers even when there is no local finding. The existing obligation gather/reduction mechanism receives all these validated facts and adjudicates cross-parent duplication once with original-file/line provenance; do not simply skip duplication coverage. Bounded reductions retain the complete note-ID/range coverage ledger and both facts needed for a candidate; no raw parent reinsertion. The pipeline may use staged bounded reduction but does not enumerate a Cartesian product of fragment pairs. Missing/foreign notes fail, not NO_EVIDENCE success. Validate counterpart references against the original changed scope. This preserves a diff-only duplication judgment rather than claiming graph symbol coverage. Every replacement revision regenerates both parent and global duplication obligations. DIFF-SCALE covers actual compare and pair execution, not just material adjacency. [c24]

Replace the daemon-authored-code degraded branch of beginDiffOnlyReview with beginControllerPipeline; never call emitJudgementsResult over whole diff grounding. Reuse prepareDimensionJob, exact fitted material, initial timing plan, modelDimensionAdapter(path:controller), requiresChunking, note validation, parent/global duplication gather and replacement revisions. Daemon prepares and validates deterministically but executes ZERO LLM judgments for this branch. Store controller-pipeline state with subject/source fingerprint, immutable snapshot, prepared jobs, serial cursor, timing, current call, revision and accepted-result ledger. Rebuild adapters from stored immutable inputs/explicit revision; verify material hash before reuse. Drive runStage for deterministic stages and expose only nextCalls()[0] from one dimension/stage at a time. Add next:emit_review_call output {state,call:{callId,dimension,stage,role,messages,schema,limitChars,expiresAt},timing}; do not return full grounding, other pending prompts or accumulated raw prior outputs. Include only the bounded explicit context/notes in that identified call. The existing judgements phase gains callResult?:{callId:string,answer?:unknown,failure?:{cause:size-refusal|invalid-answer|transient|stall,detail:string,maxChars?:number}} mutually exclusive with legacy judgements. For controller-pipeline state require exactly one callResult, exact current callId and either enveloped answer or failure; reject a complete DimensionResult[] even if valid under legacy schema. For legacy full graph state retain old whole-dimension protocol; old legacy degraded states are invalidated with restart-required and cannot bypass the new route. MCP/daemon input validation discriminates state kind and rejects mixed/foreign payloads. Apply answer through applyOutput, enforcing actual envelope/schema and semantic checks, never directly inject client verdicts as a substitute for unfinished pipeline work. Apply failure through applyFailure with bounded validated lower maxChars and existing retry rules, using singleton revision recovery when needed. Run deterministic stages to next call or complete dimension, then the next serial dimension. Advance state atomically using expected state revision/current call ID; consumed answer replay returns the cached continuation, and conflicting duplicate/foreign/out-of-order/late answers cannot rerun or overwrite work. Repeating start with controller-pipeline state returns the SAME current call and deadline, not a new call/count. Only final pipeline-derived DimensionResults may enter existing runner validation/scope filters/fold/publication, with reviewedBy:controller, client model attribution, degraded grounding/fallback reason and warn cap. No daemon provider call is used for independent controller judgment or to fill missing evidence. Recheck source author and target/fingerprint at every continuation/finalization; source changes terminate rather than silently review a new snapshot. Cancel through start/state/proceed:false, reject deadline/stale/lost states without CR; pin active state until root deadline plus terminal grace. Root clock includes controller turn waiting, child clock activates once at dimension start and per-call expiresAt=min(existing per-call allowance from first emission,child/root remaining); replay/poll never renews it. Controller has no daemon-owned subprocess to abort, so expiry revokes the call and rejects late answers. [c27] Complete-input admission also applies to controller execution: measure the entire emitted task envelope including metadata/guidance/state identifiers, messages and actual schema, reserving its framing before fit/pack; never append a second full grounding. This bounds application-provided task input, not an unknown host transcript. A bounded controller runner must use a verified fresh isolated client invocation, with no inherited conversation/project/tool context, through its locally installed CLI/OAuth abstraction. Add optional start controllerInput:{mode:isolated-structured,maxInputChars:number,adapterId:string}; this is an admission request, not proof. Resolve adapterId against a locally verified controller execution capability (same enforcing CLI isolation/normalization boundary, client-owned invocation), and use min(configured,384000,declared/verified adapter caps). Refuse unsupported-bounded-controller BEFORE returning evidence/prompts if the host cannot provide that isolation; never treat a self-declared flag or current chat history as enforcement. The daemon never substitutes its own review on this refusal. Legacy unbounded controller sessions cannot claim128K compliance. CallResult is produced by the admitted isolated controller invocation; explicit bounded history/notes are counted, and tool schema/help/guide teaches this contract. The current chat host may therefore report this route as unsupported until its verified isolated adapter is available; that is an honest pending capability, not a completed review. Concrete client enforcement lives in new src/mcp/controller-review.ts: allowlisted adapterId is cli-codex or cli-claude, implemented by the shared CliProvider enforcing fresh bounded mode. This controller-side helper verifies installed CLI isolation support, normalizes/measures the exact task and invokes that CLI locally; it never forwards the task into an existing chat/session. It drives one emitted call then sends its enveloped callResult, through the existing MCP-to-daemon step forwarding boundary. A capability descriptor comes from this actual helper, not arbitrary user JSON; unsupported hosts without the helper fail closed. Adapter selection follows the invoking controller client family and existing role/model policy; no global config mutation or direct REST. The helper stores only opaque pending controller call metadata and cancellation state, reports provider failures through the defined callResult path, and applies the same expiry/input guards before each local dispatch. It owns/aborts its subprocess on cancellation/deadline; ordinary step status waits do not relaunch it. Keep trusted helper-generated admission separate from raw tool arguments in src/mcp/server.ts and src/mcp/forward-step.ts; bypass attempts with a raw controllerInput flag cannot register a verified capability. Tests exercise this actual helper/CLI boundary with captured stdin/schema/arguments, not merely a mocked capability flag. The daemon still checks independently that the BUILD author is daemon; helper use cannot change reviewer routing.

dataModel.entity: Review input identity and publication revalidation
dataModel.details: At admission capture a canonical ReviewInputFingerprint with schemaVersion and digest over resolved target/repo identity, Story range base and HEAD, complete scoped diff content plus path/status/mode/rename/binary identities, changed-file contents needed by the grounding snapshot, effective approved contract/plan identities and content digests, and canonical review-relevant BUILD content digest including authoredBy/build revision (excluding exactly the approval/audit fields named in Shared BUILD approval freshness enforcement). Hash deterministic structured inputs; exclude timestamps/progress-only noise explicitly rather than substituting mtime for content. Snapshot capture must be consistent: compare pre/post identity while reading and retry or refuse source-changed; do not attach a fingerprint for different bytes than the snapshot. Store the admitted fingerprint and expected author in the daemon operation and controller state. Both review routes re-resolve/recompute source/contract/BUILD identity immediately before final publication even if no second start request occurs. Require author still matches independent reviewer routing; same filenames with different BUILD content, contract edits, source edits, new commits, changed uncommitted bytes or changed Story ownership all invalidate. A mismatch terminates with review-input-changed, cancels/settles owned work and writes no new CR; no auto-rebase/restart, no false completed response. Add a runner pre-publication validation hook supplied by the real RPC/controller handler (required for new timed/bounded review paths), invoked after dimension completion and immediately before the existing atomic artifact writer, under per-target operation ownership and remaining deadline/signal checks. Legacy injected direct-runner callers retain their defaults, but production new routes cannot omit the hook. Persist optional meta.reviewInputFingerprint plus reviewInputSchemaVersion on CR, required for all newly bounded/timed reviews. Do not mutate the historical S003 evidence as part of this identity. Extend enforceCodeReviewGate to recompute/compare any recorded fingerprint against current source/approved contracts/BUILD; mismatch or unavailable identity refuses the gate as stale-review even if verdict/counts are otherwise acceptable. Legacy CR without fingerprint retains explicit legacy compatibility; it is not relabeled as newly verified. This gate check closes edits after the final pre-write check, including edits between check and atomic rename, and keeps later source edits from reusing a verdict. Recheck after publication before reporting done; if identity changed in that narrow interval report stale-review/no accepted completion, leaving the fingerprinted record unusable by the gate rather than deleting another owner’s artifact. Existing previous CR is not overwritten on a mismatch detected before writing; per-target ownership prevents competing review writers. This is content identity verification, not a new index-freshness dependency. [c29] Freshness also runs at the common approveArtifactByJsonPath BUILD boundary; enforcing only the workflow wrapper is insufficient. See shared BUILD approval contract for non-overridable identity failures, outcome projection and exact canonical exclusions. The canonical input also includes separate verdict-bearing TESTS record state/content and ordering semantics as specified in Verdict-bearing TESTS input identity; source/BUILD alone is insufficient.

Add synchronous checkBuildReviewFreshness(jsonPath,buildMeta):ReviewFreshnessResult at src/workflow/gates.ts, called by approveArtifactByJsonPath for every BUILD before override handling and immediately before approvedAt/writeAtomic. Resolve repo/target from the canonical artifact-store path and validated BUILD identity; malformed/conflicting identity fails closed for a fingerprinted/new bounded CR. Reuse one synchronous canonical fingerprint reader/comparator from input-fingerprint.ts (read-only file/git operations, no LLM or client DB access), so both this synchronous common boundary and enforceCodeReviewGate judge the same identity. Result is fresh|legacy|stale-review; stale-review includes reason mismatch|unavailable|invalid and a message, not invented findings/counts. If the CR records reviewInputFingerprint/schemaVersion, validate fingerprint shape/version and current canonical source/contract/BUILD identity; malformed, unsupported-version, unreadable current identity or mismatch is stale-review. Never fall through to legacy/no-review on invalid fingerprint metadata. Legacy CR with both fingerprint fields genuinely absent retains documented old behavior; missing CR still follows mandatory independent-review rules. New timed/bounded CR publication requires both fields. A mixed partial fingerprint is invalid, not legacy. Check independent author as well as identity using the existing otherPartyReviewGap. Do not synthesize a review or call models from approval. A stale-review unconditionally throws ReviewBlockedError with summary stale-review before any approvedAt/rangeBase/reviewOverride write, tracker push, commit or follow-on; existing approval state/previous artifact remains unchanged. overrideReview and codeReview.enforce:false do NOT bypass input identity: an override may accept findings or the existing legacy missing/same-party policy, but cannot make a different source snapshot current. Error says run a new independent review, not supply an override. No new stale override field or automatic acknowledgement. [c31] Extend CodeReviewGateResult and CodeReviewApprovalOutcome with distinct status:stale-review plus reason/message and optional recorded identity; do not relabel it a block verdict or manufacture counts. enforceCodeReviewGate checks freshness BEFORE pass/warn/block and advisory/override verdict handling. approveWorkflowTarget skips both blocked and stale-review, preserving reason in codeReview outcomes; projectGateOutcome and response schema/renderers must handle the new discriminant exhaustively. The shared low-level approval check remains authoritative even when the wrapper is skipped, or inputs change between wrapper preflight and low-level write. TUI approve already calls approveArtifactByJsonPath directly: propagate the same ReviewBlockedError and withhold tracker/commit side effects; test the service entry point rather than a mock of only the wrapper. Other artifacts retain their existing policy. Include any IPC/shared/CLI outcome consumers located by direct caller/type-use search during implementation, with relevant contract tests; do not leave a default branch that accepts unknown stale status. Read/revalidate as near to atomic approval write as possible; after writing a fingerprinted BUILD approval, verify identity again before returning success or triggering tracker/follow-on. If a race is detected, restore only the prior approval metadata under the same per-target owned writer, report stale-review and run no completion side effects; never overwrite concurrent source/BUILD body edits. Later edits invalidate reuse of the recorded CR through the shared gate; they cannot turn the old review into evidence for the new snapshot. Canonical BUILD identity hashes reviewed semantic content and author, not raw artifact bytes that approval itself changes: exclude exactly meta.approvedAt, meta.rejectedAt, meta.rejectReason, meta.reviewOverride and fingerprint-derived approval outcome/audit fields; exclude no source/contract/rangeBase/task/body/author fields. Document the canonicalization version and explicit exclusions in input-fingerprint.ts; no broad metadata stripping. No-op ledger completion merges are fingerprint-stable; a substantive ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion change invalidates the prior CR and requests fresh review. Test an unchanged review -> successful BUILD approval -> reapproval without self-invalidating solely because approvedAt/audit changed. Unknown fingerprint versions cannot silently use different exclusions. No-op completion stability requires the explicit completion writer reconciliation/preservation change described in Idempotent completion BUILD ledger preservation; retaining timestamps is an actual writer change, not a new fingerprint body exclusion.

ReviewInputFingerprint includes the separately persisted TESTS record, even though ledger files are excluded from source diffs. Use the same canonical artifact path/target and testRecordState reader as resolveCodeReviewSubject, captured consistently with the subject. Encode state kind absent|record|unreadable explicitly. For record, hash the complete canonical TESTS JSON (object keys canonicalized, ARRAY ORDER PRESERVED), including all tasks, taskId, ranAt, commit, tests, files, titles/results, timeouts/exit codes, malformed nested values, builder-reported evidence and top-level metadata. Do not strip any TESTS timestamp: task ranAt determines latest-run selection, valid beats invalid, failure wins a tie, and array order can decide remaining ties. Include the actual testRecordView presented to the judge or its canonical digest alongside the record state, with BUILD task results already covered by BUILD identity; verify capture did not race. For unreadable state include deterministic reason category and available raw byte digest if readable-but-invalid; if raw input cannot be read consistently, refuse admission/publication/gate comparison as unavailable identity rather than pretending the prior TESTS evidence is current. Absent TESTS is a valid explicit state reflecting unverified coverage, not a manufactured passing test; appearance/disappearance changes identity. Presence-to-unreadable, malformed replacement, ranAt-only change that selects another run, reordered tied runs, changed titles, reported outcome/evidence and pass-to-fail all invalidate. Recompute this same identity at daemon/controller publication, shared BUILD approval and enforceCodeReviewGate. A TESTS-only persist after admission is detected without BUILD/source changes or a second start. No LLM call or manual client result can bypass these checks. TESTS remains a nonapprovable record; this adds identity verification, not approval for TESTS. [c34]

Implement the promised no-op stability in the writers; do not expand fingerprint exclusions to hide generated BUILD-body mutations. In completion-record.ts, load the valid prior BUILD before constructing the completion candidate. collectBuildChangeLog may still produce observations at now, but reconcile completion observations against prior entries by canonical target path and applicable version, retaining the prior complete author/timestamp/version entry for an unchanged target. An omitted completion version does not erase a prior known version; compare against the resolved current Story commit before preserving. Keep original deterministic ordering for unchanged entries, remove entries genuinely outside the newly scoped changed set and append genuinely new entries in deterministic collector order with new timestamps. A source-byte change in an existing file is still caught by source fingerprint even when the file-list entry is retained; this preservation never claims unchanged file contents. Define a completion-specific semantic candidate comparison after task merge, stable folder identity and resolved Story commit: compare all persisted fields except newly generated candidate meta.createdAt/meta.updatedAt and completion-observation timestamps that are explicitly reconciled back to the prior entry. Keep prior createdAt already handled by mergeWithPrior. If the resulting semantic candidate equals prior, retain prior meta.updatedAt, the exact prior body.changeLog and all prior fields; skip JSON/Markdown writes where bytes already match and return existing canonical paths. Do not refresh a known BUILD author or completion/approval fields merely because the hook ran. If tasks/results, scoped files/version, resolved Story commit, standalone/folder identity or other semantic fields actually differ, persist the substantive change with updatedAt and only genuinely new entry timestamps; the old CR must then be stale. Missing/malformed prior follows the existing fresh-record path but cannot reuse an old fingerprinted CR. Add an explicit completion mode/option to persistBuildRecord/mergeWithPrior rather than applying time suppression to genuine validate writes; default normal persistence behavior remains intact. List completion-record.ts, changed-files.ts and standalone-record.ts as production change sites. Do not mutate TESTS ranAt to obtain BUILD stability. [c35]

dataModelChanges.details: Add optional fragment provenance for file rows: parentId, part index/count, half-open UTF16 source offsets, original file identity, source/diff line-column coordinates and parent/content digests. In src/shared/types.ts add StructuredCompletionOpts.boundedInput?: { readonly maxInputChars:number; readonly contextMode:isolated-structured } | undefined and ProviderCapabilities.boundedStructuredInput?: boolean | undefined. Omitted capability means false; omitted option preserves existing behavior. The code-review driver requires advertised support before dispatch. [c15]

Add PreparedDimensionReview containing the exact immutable snapshot, adapter and prepared ReviewPipelineJob, plus dimension and primaryChunkCount. Prepare every effective dimension serially before the first LLM call, then execute the exact prepared jobs serially. Deterministic UX/diagram slots declare zero model chunks. During preparation retain the idle/stall watchdog, then reject if elapsed already exhausts the derived deadline. Planning makes no LLM calls. The immutable source snapshot and initial timing count cannot change at dispatch. Freeze root and child deadlines; retries, correction, replacement subchunks, reductions, parent gather and duplicate comparisons never increase N or reset clocks. Omission preserves legacy streaming behavior; the new step path uses operation:start. Admission resolves scope, source fingerprint and independent reviewer before creating an in-memory daemon-owned operation with opaque unguessable handle, daemon epoch, AbortController, prepared timing plan, progress and eventual outcome. One target/source fingerprint owns at most one active review: repeated start joins it; different source fingerprint for the same active target returns review-conflict instead of competing artifact writers. In pending-review state proceed:false means explicit cancellation; in existing freshness state proceed:false retains degraded diff fallback. Active operation handles are held in the runtime registry independent of the shared one-hour step token TTL/LRU. Pending continuation tokens are pinned/refreshed until operation deadline plus a 10-minute terminal grace; during preparation idle watchdog bounds lifetime. Terminal outcomes are retained for that grace then evicted, active operations are never LRU-evicted. Daemon restart reports lost operation, never completion; new review requires fresh explicit start. Only the existing validated final run writes CR, once, under ownership and signal/deadline checks. No persistent DB or new general workflow runner. [c21] [c22] In src/shared/review-stream.ts retain CodeReviewStreamResult {runId,artifact} for legacy streams, add CodeReviewControlParams as a discriminated union: start carries operation:start plus normal target/grounding fields; status/cancel carry operation and reviewHandle plus matching repo/epicHash/storyId. Extend codeReviewRequestParams to preserve validated operation/reviewHandle rather than reconstructing and dropping them. Add CodeReviewControlResult = {status:pending,reviewHandle,progress,timing?} | {status:done,reviewHandle,result:CodeReviewStreamResult} | {status:failed,reviewHandle,error,reason} | {status:cancelled,reviewHandle}. Add codeReviewControl(params,opts):Promise<CodeReviewControlResult> alongside codeReviewStream in both StepDaemonClient and socket exports; both use the same serializer and discriminate/validate terminal frame data at runtime. The existing legacy codeReviewStream remains final-only. The step switches on status: only done.result enters existing artifact/independent-review validation; pending returns continuation, failed/cancelled report no CR. runReviewStream transport cancel still closes/aborts the request waiter, but the operation-mode handler deliberately detaches this signal from operation execution; legacy stream cancellation stays unchanged. Both transports test the same request/reply fixtures, pending requires no artifact, and malformed done cannot be accepted. Final publication additionally requires fresh source/approved-contract/BUILD fingerprint and author revalidation through the mandatory production hook; see Review input identity and publication revalidation. An unchanged start handle is not proof that inputs remained current.

dataModelChanges.entity: Budget-aware diff partition and refusal recovery
dataModelChanges.details: Add fitDiffMaterial(sourceSnapshot,dimensionSpec,effectiveLimitChars,revision):ReviewMaterial in a diff-fragment material helper reused by prepareDimensionJob. The immutable snapshot retains complete parent evidence; each dimension owns a derived material view, never mutates the shared snapshot. Render the real candidate singleton chunk including complete context, parent descriptors, envelope and schema. Starting with <=16Ki staging spans, recursively halve an oversized text range at Unicode-safe boundaries, regenerate full index/count/coordinates/digests and all affected obligations/adjacency, then remeasure. Pack only after every required singleton fits. Measure fixed framing with a minimal nonempty Unicode span: if even that cannot fit, explicitly refuse irreducible context; no recursion without size progress. Initial primary count is frozen only after this fit+packing. On a provider size refusal, the existing atom-only redivide path must intercept a singleton diff fragment: derive a smaller descendant material revision from the SAME original evidence using the refused cap and the same fitting function. Restart only that dimension as a new revision/job with new call IDs, discarding its old model outputs/notes/findings (never combine old and new ownership); abort/await any owned call first. Retain frozen root/child deadlines, original primary count/budget and a replacement-lineage record. All other dimensions retain their prepared source view; execute revisions serially. Descendant IDs include original parent, absolute range and revision digest; every revision still partitions the original text without gaps/overlap. Rebuild stage closures, chunk material, obligations and parent notes consistently; adapters cannot retain stale cached material. The original primary IDs remain audit/timing provenance and map to descendant ranges, not new budget credits. Repeated refusals must strictly reduce offending text range/cap or terminate. No whole-file reread, byte loss, uncontrolled snapshot change, reused invalid notes or deadline extension. Non-diff indivisible atoms retain named AtomTooLargeError. If time expires during replacement, no completed CR. [c23]

Quality fragment rows represent ranges, not independent symbols. In code-review-duplicates.ts exclude all rows carrying diff-fragment metadata from descriptionsOf/compareStage/pairStage symbol candidates; validate/reject fragment IDs injected into those pair answers. Ordinary graph/small unfragmented symbol comparisons retain existing semantics. Do not create every sibling pair or every fragment-to-foreign-symbol pair. Parent quality adjudication explicitly checks duplication among that parent fragments using all required notes. Add one diff-duplication check-item obligation for the whole fragmented diff scope, owning every diff-fragment ID (and bounded descriptions of nonfragment changed evidence), separate from per-parent obligations. Require keyed duplication facts in each fragment note, preserving source ranges, logical behavior and potential counterpart identifiers even when there is no local finding. The existing obligation gather/reduction mechanism receives all these validated facts and adjudicates cross-parent duplication once with original-file/line provenance; do not simply skip duplication coverage. Bounded reductions retain the complete note-ID/range coverage ledger and both facts needed for a candidate; no raw parent reinsertion. The pipeline may use staged bounded reduction but does not enumerate a Cartesian product of fragment pairs. Missing/foreign notes fail, not NO_EVIDENCE success. Validate counterpart references against the original changed scope. This preserves a diff-only duplication judgment rather than claiming graph symbol coverage. Every replacement revision regenerates both parent and global duplication obligations. DIFF-SCALE covers actual compare and pair execution, not just material adjacency. [c24]

Replace the daemon-authored-code degraded branch of beginDiffOnlyReview with beginControllerPipeline; never call emitJudgementsResult over whole diff grounding. Reuse prepareDimensionJob, exact fitted material, initial timing plan, modelDimensionAdapter(path:controller), requiresChunking, note validation, parent/global duplication gather and replacement revisions. Daemon prepares and validates deterministically but executes ZERO LLM judgments for this branch. Store controller-pipeline state with subject/source fingerprint, immutable snapshot, prepared jobs, serial cursor, timing, current call, revision and accepted-result ledger. Rebuild adapters from stored immutable inputs/explicit revision; verify material hash before reuse. Drive runStage for deterministic stages and expose only nextCalls()[0] from one dimension/stage at a time. Add next:emit_review_call output {state,call:{callId,dimension,stage,role,messages,schema,limitChars,expiresAt},timing}; do not return full grounding, other pending prompts or accumulated raw prior outputs. Include only the bounded explicit context/notes in that identified call. The existing judgements phase gains callResult?:{callId:string,answer?:unknown,failure?:{cause:size-refusal|invalid-answer|transient|stall,detail:string,maxChars?:number}} mutually exclusive with legacy judgements. For controller-pipeline state require exactly one callResult, exact current callId and either enveloped answer or failure; reject a complete DimensionResult[] even if valid under legacy schema. For legacy full graph state retain old whole-dimension protocol; old legacy degraded states are invalidated with restart-required and cannot bypass the new route. MCP/daemon input validation discriminates state kind and rejects mixed/foreign payloads. Apply answer through applyOutput, enforcing actual envelope/schema and semantic checks, never directly inject client verdicts as a substitute for unfinished pipeline work. Apply failure through applyFailure with bounded validated lower maxChars and existing retry rules, using singleton revision recovery when needed. Run deterministic stages to next call or complete dimension, then the next serial dimension. Advance state atomically using expected state revision/current call ID; consumed answer replay returns the cached continuation, and conflicting duplicate/foreign/out-of-order/late answers cannot rerun or overwrite work. Repeating start with controller-pipeline state returns the SAME current call and deadline, not a new call/count. Only final pipeline-derived DimensionResults may enter existing runner validation/scope filters/fold/publication, with reviewedBy:controller, client model attribution, degraded grounding/fallback reason and warn cap. No daemon provider call is used for independent controller judgment or to fill missing evidence. Recheck source author and target/fingerprint at every continuation/finalization; source changes terminate rather than silently review a new snapshot. Cancel through start/state/proceed:false, reject deadline/stale/lost states without CR; pin active state until root deadline plus terminal grace. Root clock includes controller turn waiting, child clock activates once at dimension start and per-call expiresAt=min(existing per-call allowance from first emission,child/root remaining); replay/poll never renews it. Controller has no daemon-owned subprocess to abort, so expiry revokes the call and rejects late answers. [c27] Complete-input admission also applies to controller execution: measure the entire emitted task envelope including metadata/guidance/state identifiers, messages and actual schema, reserving its framing before fit/pack; never append a second full grounding. This bounds application-provided task input, not an unknown host transcript. A bounded controller runner must use a verified fresh isolated client invocation, with no inherited conversation/project/tool context, through its locally installed CLI/OAuth abstraction. Add optional start controllerInput:{mode:isolated-structured,maxInputChars:number,adapterId:string}; this is an admission request, not proof. Resolve adapterId against a locally verified controller execution capability (same enforcing CLI isolation/normalization boundary, client-owned invocation), and use min(configured,384000,declared/verified adapter caps). Refuse unsupported-bounded-controller BEFORE returning evidence/prompts if the host cannot provide that isolation; never treat a self-declared flag or current chat history as enforcement. The daemon never substitutes its own review on this refusal. Legacy unbounded controller sessions cannot claim128K compliance. CallResult is produced by the admitted isolated controller invocation; explicit bounded history/notes are counted, and tool schema/help/guide teaches this contract. The current chat host may therefore report this route as unsupported until its verified isolated adapter is available; that is an honest pending capability, not a completed review. Concrete client enforcement lives in new src/mcp/controller-review.ts: allowlisted adapterId is cli-codex or cli-claude, implemented by the shared CliProvider enforcing fresh bounded mode. This controller-side helper verifies installed CLI isolation support, normalizes/measures the exact task and invokes that CLI locally; it never forwards the task into an existing chat/session. It drives one emitted call then sends its enveloped callResult, through the existing MCP-to-daemon step forwarding boundary. A capability descriptor comes from this actual helper, not arbitrary user JSON; unsupported hosts without the helper fail closed. Adapter selection follows the invoking controller client family and existing role/model policy; no global config mutation or direct REST. The helper stores only opaque pending controller call metadata and cancellation state, reports provider failures through the defined callResult path, and applies the same expiry/input guards before each local dispatch. It owns/aborts its subprocess on cancellation/deadline; ordinary step status waits do not relaunch it. Keep trusted helper-generated admission separate from raw tool arguments in src/mcp/server.ts and src/mcp/forward-step.ts; bypass attempts with a raw controllerInput flag cannot register a verified capability. Tests exercise this actual helper/CLI boundary with captured stdin/schema/arguments, not merely a mocked capability flag. The daemon still checks independently that the BUILD author is daemon; helper use cannot change reviewer routing.

dataModelChanges.entity: Review input identity and publication revalidation
dataModelChanges.details: At admission capture a canonical ReviewInputFingerprint with schemaVersion and digest over resolved target/repo identity, Story range base and HEAD, complete scoped diff content plus path/status/mode/rename/binary identities, changed-file contents needed by the grounding snapshot, effective approved contract/plan identities and content digests, and canonical review-relevant BUILD content digest including authoredBy/build revision (excluding exactly the approval/audit fields named in Shared BUILD approval freshness enforcement). Hash deterministic structured inputs; exclude timestamps/progress-only noise explicitly rather than substituting mtime for content. Snapshot capture must be consistent: compare pre/post identity while reading and retry or refuse source-changed; do not attach a fingerprint for different bytes than the snapshot. Store the admitted fingerprint and expected author in the daemon operation and controller state. Both review routes re-resolve/recompute source/contract/BUILD identity immediately before final publication even if no second start request occurs. Require author still matches independent reviewer routing; same filenames with different BUILD content, contract edits, source edits, new commits, changed uncommitted bytes or changed Story ownership all invalidate. A mismatch terminates with review-input-changed, cancels/settles owned work and writes no new CR; no auto-rebase/restart, no false completed response. Add a runner pre-publication validation hook supplied by the real RPC/controller handler (required for new timed/bounded review paths), invoked after dimension completion and immediately before the existing atomic artifact writer, under per-target operation ownership and remaining deadline/signal checks. Legacy injected direct-runner callers retain their defaults, but production new routes cannot omit the hook. Persist optional meta.reviewInputFingerprint plus reviewInputSchemaVersion on CR, required for all newly bounded/timed reviews. Do not mutate the historical S003 evidence as part of this identity. Extend enforceCodeReviewGate to recompute/compare any recorded fingerprint against current source/approved contracts/BUILD; mismatch or unavailable identity refuses the gate as stale-review even if verdict/counts are otherwise acceptable. Legacy CR without fingerprint retains explicit legacy compatibility; it is not relabeled as newly verified. This gate check closes edits after the final pre-write check, including edits between check and atomic rename, and keeps later source edits from reusing a verdict. Recheck after publication before reporting done; if identity changed in that narrow interval report stale-review/no accepted completion, leaving the fingerprinted record unusable by the gate rather than deleting another owner’s artifact. Existing previous CR is not overwritten on a mismatch detected before writing; per-target ownership prevents competing review writers. This is content identity verification, not a new index-freshness dependency. [c29] Freshness also runs at the common approveArtifactByJsonPath BUILD boundary; enforcing only the workflow wrapper is insufficient. See shared BUILD approval contract for non-overridable identity failures, outcome projection and exact canonical exclusions. The canonical input also includes separate verdict-bearing TESTS record state/content and ordering semantics as specified in Verdict-bearing TESTS input identity; source/BUILD alone is insufficient.

Add synchronous checkBuildReviewFreshness(jsonPath,buildMeta):ReviewFreshnessResult at src/workflow/gates.ts, called by approveArtifactByJsonPath for every BUILD before override handling and immediately before approvedAt/writeAtomic. Resolve repo/target from the canonical artifact-store path and validated BUILD identity; malformed/conflicting identity fails closed for a fingerprinted/new bounded CR. Reuse one synchronous canonical fingerprint reader/comparator from input-fingerprint.ts (read-only file/git operations, no LLM or client DB access), so both this synchronous common boundary and enforceCodeReviewGate judge the same identity. Result is fresh|legacy|stale-review; stale-review includes reason mismatch|unavailable|invalid and a message, not invented findings/counts. If the CR records reviewInputFingerprint/schemaVersion, validate fingerprint shape/version and current canonical source/contract/BUILD identity; malformed, unsupported-version, unreadable current identity or mismatch is stale-review. Never fall through to legacy/no-review on invalid fingerprint metadata. Legacy CR with both fingerprint fields genuinely absent retains documented old behavior; missing CR still follows mandatory independent-review rules. New timed/bounded CR publication requires both fields. A mixed partial fingerprint is invalid, not legacy. Check independent author as well as identity using the existing otherPartyReviewGap. Do not synthesize a review or call models from approval. A stale-review unconditionally throws ReviewBlockedError with summary stale-review before any approvedAt/rangeBase/reviewOverride write, tracker push, commit or follow-on; existing approval state/previous artifact remains unchanged. overrideReview and codeReview.enforce:false do NOT bypass input identity: an override may accept findings or the existing legacy missing/same-party policy, but cannot make a different source snapshot current. Error says run a new independent review, not supply an override. No new stale override field or automatic acknowledgement. [c31] Extend CodeReviewGateResult and CodeReviewApprovalOutcome with distinct status:stale-review plus reason/message and optional recorded identity; do not relabel it a block verdict or manufacture counts. enforceCodeReviewGate checks freshness BEFORE pass/warn/block and advisory/override verdict handling. approveWorkflowTarget skips both blocked and stale-review, preserving reason in codeReview outcomes; projectGateOutcome and response schema/renderers must handle the new discriminant exhaustively. The shared low-level approval check remains authoritative even when the wrapper is skipped, or inputs change between wrapper preflight and low-level write. TUI approve already calls approveArtifactByJsonPath directly: propagate the same ReviewBlockedError and withhold tracker/commit side effects; test the service entry point rather than a mock of only the wrapper. Other artifacts retain their existing policy. Include any IPC/shared/CLI outcome consumers located by direct caller/type-use search during implementation, with relevant contract tests; do not leave a default branch that accepts unknown stale status. Read/revalidate as near to atomic approval write as possible; after writing a fingerprinted BUILD approval, verify identity again before returning success or triggering tracker/follow-on. If a race is detected, restore only the prior approval metadata under the same per-target owned writer, report stale-review and run no completion side effects; never overwrite concurrent source/BUILD body edits. Later edits invalidate reuse of the recorded CR through the shared gate; they cannot turn the old review into evidence for the new snapshot. Canonical BUILD identity hashes reviewed semantic content and author, not raw artifact bytes that approval itself changes: exclude exactly meta.approvedAt, meta.rejectedAt, meta.rejectReason, meta.reviewOverride and fingerprint-derived approval outcome/audit fields; exclude no source/contract/rangeBase/task/body/author fields. Document the canonicalization version and explicit exclusions in input-fingerprint.ts; no broad metadata stripping. No-op ledger completion merges are fingerprint-stable; a substantive ensureBuildRecordOnCompletion change invalidates the prior CR and requests fresh review. Test an unchanged review -> successful BUILD approval -> reapproval without self-invalidating solely because approvedAt/audit changed. Unknown fingerprint versions cannot silently use different exclusions. No-op completion stability requires the explicit completion writer reconciliation/preservation change described in Idempotent completion BUILD ledger preservation; retaining timestamps is an actual writer change, not a new fingerprint body exclusion.

ReviewInputFingerprint includes the separately persisted TESTS record, even though ledger files are excluded from source diffs. Use the same canonical artifact path/target and testRecordState reader as resolveCodeReviewSubject, captured consistently with the subject. Encode state kind absent|record|unreadable explicitly. For record, hash the complete canonical TESTS JSON (object keys canonicalized, ARRAY ORDER PRESERVED), including all tasks, taskId, ranAt, commit, tests, files, titles/results, timeouts/exit codes, malformed nested values, builder-reported evidence and top-level metadata. Do not strip any TESTS timestamp: task ranAt determines latest-run selection, valid beats invalid, failure wins a tie, and array order can decide remaining ties. Include the actual testRecordView presented to the judge or its canonical digest alongside the record state, with BUILD task results already covered by BUILD identity; verify capture did not race. For unreadable state include deterministic reason category and available raw byte digest if readable-but-invalid; if raw input cannot be read consistently, refuse admission/publication/gate comparison as unavailable identity rather than pretending the prior TESTS evidence is current. Absent TESTS is a valid explicit state reflecting unverified coverage, not a manufactured passing test; appearance/disappearance changes identity. Presence-to-unreadable, malformed replacement, ranAt-only change that selects another run, reordered tied runs, changed titles, reported outcome/evidence and pass-to-fail all invalidate. Recompute this same identity at daemon/controller publication, shared BUILD approval and enforceCodeReviewGate. A TESTS-only persist after admission is detected without BUILD/source changes or a second start. No LLM call or manual client result can bypass these checks. TESTS remains a nonapprovable record; this adds identity verification, not approval for TESTS. [c34]

Implement the promised no-op stability in the writers; do not expand fingerprint exclusions to hide generated BUILD-body mutations. In completion-record.ts, load the valid prior BUILD before constructing the completion candidate. collectBuildChangeLog may still produce observations at now, but reconcile completion observations against prior entries by canonical target path and applicable version, retaining the prior complete author/timestamp/version entry for an unchanged target. An omitted completion version does not erase a prior known version; compare against the resolved current Story commit before preserving. Keep original deterministic ordering for unchanged entries, remove entries genuinely outside the newly scoped changed set and append genuinely new entries in deterministic collector order with new timestamps. A source-byte change in an existing file is still caught by source fingerprint even when the file-list entry is retained; this preservation never claims unchanged file contents. Define a completion-specific semantic candidate comparison after task merge, stable folder identity and resolved Story commit: compare all persisted fields except newly generated candidate meta.createdAt/meta.updatedAt and completion-observation timestamps that are explicitly reconciled back to the prior entry. Keep prior createdAt already handled by mergeWithPrior. If the resulting semantic candidate equals prior, retain prior meta.updatedAt, the exact prior body.changeLog and all prior fields; skip JSON/Markdown writes where bytes already match and return existing canonical paths. Do not refresh a known BUILD author or completion/approval fields merely because the hook ran. If tasks/results, scoped files/version, resolved Story commit, standalone/folder identity or other semantic fields actually differ, persist the substantive change with updatedAt and only genuinely new entry timestamps; the old CR must then be stale. Missing/malformed prior follows the existing fresh-record path but cannot reuse an old fingerprinted CR. Add an explicit completion mode/option to persistBuildRecord/mergeWithPrior rather than applying time suppression to genuine validate writes; default normal persistence behavior remains intact. List completion-record.ts, changed-files.ts and standalone-record.ts as production change sites. Do not mutate TESTS ranAt to obtain BUILD stability. [c35]

errorCases.scenario: Captured diff is incomplete or truncated before span creation.
errorCases.detection: Existing reader truncation/missing-hunk markers or captured byte totals show unavailable evidence.
errorCases.response: Recover complete per-file evidence through the existing reader where possible; otherwise stop before a completed review and name the affected file/read limit. Never present omitted entries as reviewed.
errorCases.userImpact: Review remains pending until evidence can be read completely; no inventory or release-gate changes.

errorCases.scenario: Fragment ranges are missing, duplicated, reordered or inconsistent with the captured parent.
errorCases.detection: Validate parent digest, part count/order and contiguous half-open offsets; reassembly digest differs from the original.
errorCases.response: Reject material before model calls; no partial review artifact.
errorCases.userImpact: A concrete evidence-integrity error identifies the parent file.

errorCases.scenario: Complete call becomes larger than the128K budget after schema, context, history or repair additions.
errorCases.detection: The shared measurer and final normalized provider check exceed min(configured limit,384000 characters) for the actual call.
errorCases.response: Use existing redivision/reduction to create smaller complete calls; if fixed required context/schema itself cannot fit, fail explicitly. Never drop required context, resend unchanged or raise the budget.
errorCases.userImpact: More bounded serial calls, or an explicit irreducible-input error with no review stamped.

errorCases.scenario: Provider cannot prevent unmeasured session/project/tool context in bounded structured mode.
errorCases.detection: The provider lacks a verified isolation capability or cannot normalize/count its supplied instructions/schema before spawn.
errorCases.response: Refuse that bounded execution mode before the model call; do not claim the128K invariant was enforced.
errorCases.userImpact: Select/update a supported CLI adapter; ordinary completions outside this mode retain existing behavior.

errorCases.scenario: Cancellation, missing chunk answer or gather validation failure.
errorCases.detection: Existing signal/deadline checks or provenance validation notice unfinished required calls/notes. Parent-file gather also compares validated note provenance with the expected fragment set.
errorCases.response: Preserve existing stop/fail semantics; no fabricated complete verdict and no parallel retry. Missing parent evidence never uses the generic no-evidence-success branch.
errorCases.userImpact: Review stays pending with its actual failure cause.

errorCases.scenario: Derived review deadline expires, explicit cancellation, or idle/stall failure.
errorCases.detection: Injectable monotonic elapsed clock/absolute deadline and existing progress watchdog; distinguish deadline from idle and cancel.
errorCases.response: Abort owned execution, reject late output and publish no completed CR. Preserve terminal cause for bounded status retrieval; polling cannot reset timers.
errorCases.userImpact: Review remains pending with counts, elapsed time and failure cause.

errorCases.scenario: Host wait ends, duplicate start, stale handle, restart or changed source during an active review.
errorCases.detection: Daemon-owned operation registry validates handle, epoch, target and source fingerprint.
errorCases.response: Detach waiter without cancelling the review; same source joins, changed source conflicts. Missing/restarted operation is explicitly lost, never a fabricated success. Explicit cancel stops the real operation.
errorCases.userImpact: Resume the same review through returned state; start afresh only after terminal/lost state is reported.

errorCases.scenario: Controller review host cannot enforce fresh bounded execution or submits a legacy whole-dimension verdict for fragmented diff.
errorCases.detection: Verified isolated adapter admission, state-kind dispatch, call identity/schema/provenance and deadline checks.
errorCases.response: Refuse unsupported host before evidence emission; otherwise reject invalid result and retain only valid pipeline state under original deadline. Never reroute daemon-authored code to daemon judgment.
errorCases.userImpact: Controller review remains pending with exact capability or validation cause; no false128K claim or CR.

errorCases.scenario: Source, approved contract or BUILD identity/author changes while review is running or before its gate is consumed.
errorCases.detection: Canonical admitted content identity is compared at final publication and gate evaluation; no second start is necessary.
errorCases.response: Before writing, terminate review-input-changed without a new CR. If the source changes after publication check, fingerprint validation refuses stale gate consumption and post-publication check reports no accepted completion.
errorCases.userImpact: Fresh independent review is required for the changed inputs; the old verdict cannot authorize the current Story.

errorCases.scenario: Stale fingerprinted CR reaches direct/TUI BUILD approval, including with findings override or enforcement disabled.
errorCases.detection: Shared approveArtifactByJsonPath identity check and final pre-write revalidation; workflow wrapper reports the same distinct stale-review status.
errorCases.response: Refuse without approval/follow-on/tracker/commit side effects; input identity cannot be overridden by accepting review findings. Report new independent review required.
errorCases.userImpact: Both approval entry points consistently withhold completion for the changed Story.

edgeCases.input: Empty diff, binary file or small ordinary text file.
edgeCases.expected: Existing markers and single-file row behavior remain compatible; no invented graph coverage.

edgeCases.input: Pretty/minified JSON, one line far larger than a call, CRLF, emoji and non-ASCII paths.
edgeCases.expected: Unicode-safe span continuation preserves the exact evidence string, coordinates and deterministic ordered IDs; later chunks never treat an isolated fragment as a whole valid JSON document.

edgeCases.input: Added/deleted/renamed files or lines existing only on the old side.
edgeCases.expected: Original old/new paths and coordinates remain attributable; changedFiles is unique and findings stay within the original Story scope.

edgeCases.input: Many fragments in the same file/module.
edgeCases.expected: Sparse sibling connectivity and parent gather avoid new quadratic fragment-pair generation while retaining all fragment notes/provenance.

edgeCases.input: Existing configured review limit above128K or below it.
edgeCases.expected: Diff calls use the lower of configured limit and128K; schema/context reserve consumes that budget rather than increasing it.

edgeCases.input: A final gather or correction contains large prior notes/history.
edgeCases.expected: Existing bounded reduction/gather plans include those actual notes/history in measurement; no hidden accumulated transcript is resumed.

edgeCases.input: Fragmented diff whose complete quality prompt fits one call.
edgeCases.expected: requiresChunking explicitly selects measured chunk mode and parent gather; a single planned chunk is still plan.single:false and must produce parent notes.

edgeCases.input: 1, 5 or 20 initial chunks; retries, split replacement chunks, zero-model dimensions, huge/invalid count or multi-hour review.
edgeCases.expected: 10, 50 or 200 minutes respectively, per-dimension sums explicit. Retry/splits never extend; deterministic slots count zero; invalid/overflow values fail admission and long timers use slices. One fitting primary call counts one.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Original changed-file scope, independent daemon reviewer and degraded diff result cap stay intact.
Existing source-symbol identities and eligible graph coverage remain unchanged; fragment rows carry no invented call/test edges.
Existing serial prepare/review/gather, cancellation and complete failure semantics are reused.
All supplied input under one128K estimate includes envelopes, schema, explicit context and history; no budget increase is an implementation workaround.
S003 evidence contents and disabled release state remain unchanged; its earlier foundation/service coverage is not silently cleared.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test + node:assert/strict via Node22/tsx; extend the existing code-review and review-pipeline *.test.ts suites identified in s1. CLI transport isolation uses subprocess fixtures rather than a live model for deterministic limit checks.

testLevels.purpose: Prove complete evidence partition and attribution, including a minified line larger than the128K call budget.
subjects: DIFF-SPANS: added/modified/deleted/renamed text and binary/small-file compatibility; reassembly equals original diff exactly
DIFF-COORDS: CRLF, emoji, Unicode and giant-line continuations preserve offsets/old-new source locations and unique changedFiles
DIFF-INTEGRITY: duplicate/missing/reordered span and digest mismatches reject before calls
fixturesNeeded: Deterministic multi-megabyte pretty/minified inventory-style JSON and mixed unified diffs; do not rewrite the real S003 audit data.

testLevels.purpose: Prove the128K limit covers the entire sent call and all accumulated supplied context/history.
subjects: DIFF-BUDGET: at/below/above128000×3 with message role separators, call envelope, actual schema, examples, neighbour context and assistant/history content
DIFF-REPAIR: added correction/history causes smaller redivision/reduction or an explicit refusal; no oversized call is sent
DIFF-TRANSPORT: provider normalization/schema expansion and isolated fresh-call mode are measured; unmeasured project/tool/session additions are disabled or refused

DIFF-ADMISSION: absent/false boundedStructuredInput support yields zero completion calls; declared support receives the exact shared boundedInput shape and authoritative job.plan.limitChars for all chunk/gather/repair requests.
fixturesNeeded: Independent captured stdin/schema and invocation-argument assertions for configured CLI adapters; include sentinel project/history inputs and a no-child-spawn oversized control.

testLevels.purpose: Exercise existing prepare/review/gather across every fragment and final bounded call.
subjects: DIFF-LARGE: S003-sized inventory evidence produces multiple serial review calls under384000 complete-input characters; every source span is carried by a completed chunk
DIFF-GATHER: gather combines findings and provenance across parent-file fragments; no fragment omitted, out-of-scope finding promoted, or graph coverage invented
DIFF-SCALE: many fragments retain sparse sibling connectivity and avoid new quadratic material construction
DIFF-COMPAT: source-symbol and small-file review parity, cancellation, retries, gather/reduction, duplicate comparisons, and lower configured budgets remain supported

DIFF-PARENT-QUALITY: no chunk emits a local finding; a parent correctness finding is produced only when gather receives facts from two separate fragments. Reject missing/foreign/duplicate parent notes and prove reduction preserves both facts and provenance.

DIFF-READER: through DiffGroundingDeps/git-diff reader, recover truncated per-file input completely or refuse unrecoverable truncation/missing hunks before any model call or completed artifact. Replace the legacy tests that explicitly allow truncated bounded-slice reviews.

DIFF-FACTORY-LIMIT: for each of the five model-dimension factories, a provider cap below configured review size reaches adapter reduction/duplicate budgets, createJob.plan.limitChars and every boundedInput.maxInputChars unchanged. Cover the two deterministic callers without introducing a separate budget.

DIFF-FITS-ONE-CALL: a file larger than16Ki with complete prompt below128K still forces quality chunk mode, validates one note per fragment and executes parent gather. Ordinary non-fragment input remains single-call compatible.
fixturesNeeded: Scripted structured model records actual complete calls and emits bounded valid chunk/gather answers; no fake PASS from missing evidence.

migration.backwardCompat: Internal additive metadata/options only. Rows without fragment provenance retain legacy semantics, and graph-based source-symbol identities and existing review result shapes remain compatible. No new IPC method or persistent domain schema. Existing codeReview.run gains optional operation/handle fields and control-frame responses for opted-in clients; absent operation retains legacy streaming. Existing step phases stay unchanged; pending-review next/state is additive and its cancellation semantics are documented. Existing pending jobs with old whole-file snapshots are restarted as new jobs; no in-place job rewrite or fabricated continuation. Non-review CLI completions retain defaults; bounded diff calls fail explicitly if isolation cannot be enforced. For daemon-authored degraded reviews, new emit_review_call/callResult variants replace emit_judgements; old degraded tokens require restart and cannot accept direct dimension verdicts. Legacy full-graph controller review remains compatible. Bounded controller execution requires a verified isolated host adapter or fails before evidence emission. New bounded/timed CRs carry an optional additive content fingerprint checked by the existing gate; legacy records without it retain legacy behavior and are not represented as satisfying the new identity guarantee.

alternativesConsidered.name: Attributable diff spans in the existing chunk pipeline
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Represent file diffs as ordered bounded source spans, then reuse existing chunk review and gather with complete-call size checks.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep one parent file identity and add complete ordered diff-span metadata to its review rows. Plain text, JSON, additions and removals use the same evidence contract; no file must be a single indivisible atom. Every span retains original evidence and source coordinates, and file-level gather judges across span notes. All context and carried history enter explicitly constructed, freshly measured calls under the128K budget; no ambient conversational transcript is carried. Existing source-symbol graph reviews and independent reviewer selection remain intact.
pros: Smallest complete change at the broken file-to-atom boundary.
Works for pretty and minified JSON and other text without inventing a format-specific semantic parser.
Reuses serial review, gather, retries and degraded-coverage reporting.
cons: Continuation spans must expose clear context and offsets, especially for a single very long line.
All file-level consumers must handle one-to-many rows and preserve attribution/completeness.

alternativesConsidered.name: JSON entry review units with a generic diff fallback
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Give JSON object/array entries explicit semantic units and use source spans for non-JSON or oversized values.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Model JSON parent containers and entry identities explicitly, with source coordinates and before/after evidence; review entries independently and gather at the parent. Other diff text and oversized scalar values require the generic bounded-span contract as a fallback. Both paths measure complete rendered calls including schema, context, notes and correction/history under128K, and retain independent degraded review.
pros: Semantic JSON keys make inventory-entry context clearer.
Per-container gather can express relationships among generated entries.
cons: Adds parsing and before/after correspondence rules for arbitrary JSON, duplicate keys and malformed inputs.
Still needs generic spans for giant strings, minified values and non-JSON diffs, creating two attribution paths.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Also meets the constraints but adds a JSON-specific data model while still requiring generic spans for minified giant values; more implementation and compatibility risk without additional requested capability.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The sequence shows where complete diff evidence is divided and where all supplied context/history/schema must be counted before a serial model call. Parent-file provenance flows through every chunk into gather; the budget guard can stop a call without dropping evidence. Preparation freezes primary chunk counts and 10-minute-per-chunk budgets before any model call; all later work consumes the same deadline. A daemon-owned operation outlives a bounded status waiter. For daemon-authored code, the controller supplies each identified bounded answer instead of the CLI-provider lifeline; the daemon only prepares/validates that serial protocol, preserves controller authorship and refuses a host without verified isolated execution.

participants.label: Snapshot
participants.description: Owns original per-file text and change-set provenance; no source is reread mid-review.

participants.label: Diff spans

participants.label: Planner
participants.description: Groups complete spans and explicit neighbour/context notes into measurable calls. Prepares exact jobs/counts before execution and freezes aggregate/child timing.

participants.label: Input guard
participants.description: Counts envelopes, actual schema, context, history and correction content against the128K cap. Also enforces remaining immutable deadline before dispatch and after completion.

participants.label: CLI provider
participants.description: One fresh CLI-backed request at a time; no unmeasured conversational or tool history.

participants.label: Parent gather
participants.description: Collects all fragment findings and notes, reduces bounded context and preserves degraded review semantics.

messages.label: Capture diff + identity
messages.description: Read limits/incomplete evidence cannot be hidden by chunking.

messages.label: Complete attributed spans
messages.description: The parent owns every span; source ranges reconstruct the captured diff.

messages.label: Full request + schema
messages.description: Payload-only size is insufficient; all added material consumes the same cap. Freeze initial primary count N and 600000*N allowance; root aggregates dimensions and includes post-admission preparation.

messages.label: Fit check, then submit
messages.description: Oversized calls are redivided/reduced or refused before dispatch. Submit with min(per-call timeout, child remaining, root remaining); late answers cannot finalize.

messages.label: Facts + provenance
messages.description: Return one validated parent-obligation evidence note per carried fragment, plus local findings/descriptions.

messages.label: Bounded parent evidence
messages.description: Require every parent fragment note, reduce context with provenance when needed, then adjudicate correctness across fragments.

messages.label: Check context/history
messages.description: The same guard applies to every later call, not only initial chunks.

messages.label: Next isolated call
messages.description: No opaque session transcript is resumed. Same fixed deadline; retry, gather and redivision do not extend it. Bounded status waits retain the same operation.

messages.label: Parent judgement
messages.description: Keep parent-file attribution and existing independent/degraded verdict limits.
